With homegap.tls: terminate on the front door, HomeGAP uses Pangolin HTTP resources for the root and the wildcard. The node ends TLS and sends the request again to the homelab Traefik. The request keeps its host.

The nodes hold a certificate for the root name. With homegap.wildcard, they also hold a certificate for *.<domain>. HomeGAP then refuses passthrough on other hostnames under the domain. See Certificates.

Wildcard HTTP resources are a Pangolin EE feature, so every node needs a license. See Pangolin EE licenses. If a node refuses the wildcard, HomeGAP removes that node from the wildcard DNS set. Thus viewers never go to a node that answers 404.

To compare the two modes, change this one label. Use terminate when you need Pangolin sign-in or CrowdSec.

items.title: Dedicated hostname
items.text:
A labeled service with its own hostname gets its own resource. This resource has priority over the wildcard. A public service also gets its own geo DNS record set.

An https service uses passthrough by default, directly to the service. It has its own SNI route with a higher priority than the front door. The node terminates plain http services.

items.title: Health resource
items.text:
Each node gets a health resource, hg-health. In cluster mode, its name is hg-health-<node id>. Its hostname is homegap-health-<node id>.<domain>.

The health resource goes to the front door. If there is no front door, it goes to the first dedicated http or https service. The request has the host header of that service and the path from its homegap.healthcheck (default /). The Bunny monitor on port 80 reaches this resource.

items.title: When the homelab is down
items.text:
A node shows a "back shortly" page with HTTP status 503 for the names that it terminates:

  • Each service with homegap.tls: terminate. To disable the page for a service, set homegap.maintenance_page: "false".
  • The shared names of the status page and the speed test.

The page starts approximately 15 seconds after the node loses the homelab.

A passthrough name has no page, because the node holds no certificate for it. The node closes the connection immediately, and the browser shows a connection error. The shared name of the status page tells your users that the homelab is unreachable. Raw ports fail.

items.title: When a browser uses one connection for two names
items.text:
The names on a node have the same IP address. If one certificate is valid for two of them, a browser can use one connection for both names. For example, Firefox opens pangolin.example.net and then sends the requests for app.example.net on the same connection. But the node ends TLS for pangolin.example.net and uses passthrough for app.example.net. Without a correction, the wrong Traefik gets the request and answers 404.

HomeGAP makes each Traefik answer 421 (Misdirected Request) for these requests. The browser then opens a new connection for the name, and the request goes to the correct location.

  • On each node, the route homegap-misdirected matches the names that the node passes through. HomeGAP writes it in the routes file of the node.
  • On the homelab, the route homegap-misdirected matches the names that only the nodes serve: the management host of each node, the client address, and the shared names of the status page and the speed test. Traefik gets this route from the orchestrator through its HTTP provider. See step 14 of Install on the homelab. HomeGAP does not include a name that your homelab Traefik routes itself, when it can read the routes of your Traefik. If it cannot read them, it does not include the shared name of the speed test.

Each of these routes uses its own TLS options, homegap-elsewhere. Traefik answers 421 when the TLS options of the route are different from the TLS options of the connection. On a connection for the correct name, no other route matches, and the request goes to its usual route.

A service that ends TLS itself, with no Traefik in front of it, cannot answer 421. If a browser uses the connection of such a service for another name, the service gets the request.

items.title: Comparison
items.text: Passthrough Terminate What the node sees Only the SNI. Plaintext. Where TLS ends On the homelab Traefik, or on the service. On the node. Certificates on the node None for your services. A certificate for each name. See Certificates. Maintenance page Not possible. Enabled by default. EE license Not necessary. Necessary for wildcard resources. Pangolin sign-in Not possible. Possible. CrowdSec Not possible. Possible.

items.title: Fluxer (chat and voice)
items.text: Fluxer is a self-hosted chat app. Its voice and video calls use a bundled LiveKit server. This page tells you how to publish Fluxer through HomeGAP, with the call media on raw ports.

items.title: How Fluxer uses the network
items.text:
Fluxer uses one domain (FLUXER_DOMAIN). The web app, the API, the gateway and the voice signalling share this domain by path (/api/, /gateway and /livekit). Thus the front door publishes all of them, through your homelab Traefik.

The call media does not use the domain. It goes directly to LiveKit on TCP 7881 and UDP 7882 (FLUXER_LIVEKIT_TCP_PORT and FLUXER_LIVEKIT_UDP_PORT). LiveKit tells the clients a literal address (FLUXER_LIVEKIT_NODE_IP, with FLUXER_LIVEKIT_USE_EXTERNAL_IP=false). The public port must be the same as the container port.

This page gives two setups:

Setup Calls Failover for calls Direct media through one node LiveKit advertises the address of one node. No. TURN (recommended for several nodes) Callers reach a TURN server by name, on the nearest healthy node. Yes.

items.title: What the tests checked
items.text:
Both setups pass the end-to-end tests in the HomeGAP harness, through each of two nodes. The tests check the web app, the signalling and the media path.

The tests do not check a call between two users of the Fluxer app. The API of Fluxer disconnects LiveKit participants that do not join through Fluxer ("participant_joined without usable metadata"). Thus the tests use plain LiveKit clients, and run LiveKit without the webhook of Fluxer.

items.title: The web app
items.text:
1. Put Fluxer in proxy mode. In the .env of Fluxer, set this value: 
    COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.yml:docker-compose.proxy.yml
    In proxy mode, the edge of Fluxer listens on plain HTTP port 8080 for your proxy. FLUXER_EDGE_BIND sets the address on the host.
  2. Attach the edge service of Fluxer to the Traefik network, in a compose override of Fluxer: 
    services:
  edge:
    networks: [fluxer, traefik]

networks:
  traefik:
    external: true
  3. Route chat.example.net from your homelab Traefik to the edge, for example in the dynamic config: 
    http:
  routers:
    fluxer:
      rule: "Host(`chat.example.net`)"
      entryPoints: [websecure]
      service: fluxer
      tls: {}
  services:
    fluxer:
      loadBalancer:
        servers:
          - url: "http://fluxer-edge-1:8080"
    Replace fluxer-edge-1 with the name of the edge container.

The front door publishes chat.example.net. The web app needs no HomeGAP labels.

The proxy requirements of Fluxer apply to your Traefik as usual: WebSocket upgrades, long timeouts and bodies up to 512 MB. See the reverse proxy guide of Fluxer.

items.title: The network of LiveKit
items.text:
The tunnels container must join the Docker network of Fluxer. With the project name fluxer, this network is fluxer_fluxer. Add it to the tunnels service in the homelab compose file:

services:
  tunnels:
    networks: [traefik, fluxer]

networks:
  fluxer:
    external: true
    name: fluxer_fluxer

You can also use docker network connect fluxer_fluxer <tunnels container>.

Caution

LiveKit must be on one Docker network only: the network that it shares with tunnels (or with coturn). On two networks, LiveKit answers from its address on one network, while the packets of the tunnel arrive at the other. Then calls fail with "could not connect". The order of the interfaces can change on each restart. Thus join tunnels to the network of Fluxer. Do not add a network to LiveKit.

items.title: Setup 1: direct media through one node
items.text:
In this setup, all calls go through one node. It is the simpler setup, but calls have no failover.

  1. In a compose override of Fluxer, remove the published ports of the livekit service, and add the labels: 
    services:
  livekit:
    ports: !reset []
    labels:
      homegap.expose: "voice.example.net"
      homegap.port: "7881/tcp, 7882/udp"
      homegap.regions: "na1"
  2. In the .env of Fluxer, set the public IPv4 address of that node: 
    FLUXER_LIVEKIT_NODE_IP=203.0.113.10
FLUXER_LIVEKIT_USE_EXTERNAL_IP=false
  3. Restart Fluxer.

We recommend homegap.regions with the advertised node, so that HomeGAP publishes the ports only there. With all nodes, calls still use only the advertised node.

In the test, a call has one audio publisher, one video publisher and two subscribers. All 4 of 4 tracks arrive, with approximately 1.2 Mbps of video each and 0% packet loss, in three runs out of three. The selected ICE pair of LiveKit is the node address on 7882/udp, with the remote end at the tunnels container.

items.title: Setup 2: TURN
items.text:
In this setup, calls reach a TURN server by name. DNS sends each caller to the nearest healthy node, so failover also works for calls. We recommend it when you have several nodes.

  1. Add coturn on the network of Fluxer, in a compose override of Fluxer: 
    services:
  turn:
    image: docker.io/coturn/coturn:4.7.0
    command:
      - --listening-port=3478
      - --realm=example.net
      - --use-auth-secret
      - --static-auth-secret=<secret>
      - --min-port=49160
      - --max-port=49200
      - --allowed-peer-ip=<the Docker network range of LiveKit>
      - --no-tls
      - --no-dtls
      - --no-cli
      - --fingerprint
    networks: [fluxer]
    labels:
      homegap.expose: "turn.example.net"
      homegap.port: "3478/tcp+udp"
  2. In the .env of Fluxer, set the TURN servers. Use the same secret as coturn: 
    FLUXER_LIVEKIT_TURN_SERVERS='[{"host":"turn.example.net","port":3478,"protocol":"udp","secret":"<secret>"},{"host":"turn.example.net","port":3478,"protocol":"tcp","secret":"<secret>"}]'
  3. In the same file, leave the node address empty: 
    FLUXER_LIVEKIT_NODE_IP=
FLUXER_LIVEKIT_USE_EXTERNAL_IP=false
  4. Make sure that the livekit service has no HomeGAP labels and no published ports.
  5. Restart Fluxer.

LiveKit then advertises its container address, and only coturn can reach it. With a secret, coturn checks short-lived credentials (use-auth-secret). The host of a TURN server can be a hostname.

In the test, each of the two nodes gives 4 of 4 tracks with 0% loss. coturn logs 24 successful allocations and 168 channel binds, all from the address of the tunnels container.
